title: Adaptive quantization + prompt sprint notes for Retail POC
summary: Working notes from a focused sprint to converge on a production-feasible model + quantization + prompt pipeline for the retail customer POC. Emphasis: keep p95 latency < 220ms for short chat turns, maintain semantic fidelity for SKU matching and instruction-following, and iterate on lightweight prompt templates and small retrieval passes.
objective: Deliver an inference configuration that balances cost and latency while preserving SKU matching accuracy and natural language instruction compliance for chat and quick product search workflows.
background_and_constraints: Customer runs in EU, needs VPC private deployment option. Sensitive PII in support transcripts must not be uploaded to third-party. They require predictable latency for storefront chat (p95 <= 220ms) and budget target ~ $0.003 per 1k tokens generation. They prefer open models but will accept a Redwood-verified curated variant.
model_candidates: Evaluated: Llama2-13B, Falcon-40B-instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, a trimmed 7B SFT from partner. Initial priority: Mistral-7B-Instruct (base) and Llama2-13B-quant for accuracy baseline.
quantization_options_considered: 1) fp16 baseline (dev only) 2) dynamic 8-bit (int8) for 13B 3) 4-bit (q4_k_m / q4_0) for 7B options 4) mixed mode: KV cache and attention keys in 8-bit, weights in 4-bit for hot-path models
microbench_results:
Test harness: 1k typical retail turns (avg 22 tokens output). Hardware: a2-48g equivalent. Results (median of 10 runs):
- Mistral-7B fp16: p95 190ms, throughput 28 rps, relative quality baseline 1.00
- Mistral-7B q4_0: p95 140ms, throughput 40 rps, quality 0.98 (small drop on SKU fuzzy-match)
- Llama2-13B int8: p95 260ms, throughput 18 rps, quality 1.04 (better factual precision)
- Llama2-13B q8_dyn: p95 210ms, throughput 22 rps, quality 1.02
Notes: q4_0 on 7B is the strongest single-node latency win. 13B in int8 still struggles to meet p95 target on single reserved slot, but gives higher accuracy on edge cases.
prompt_pipeline_design: 1) Retrieval: small vector store of 10 nearest-context items (customer support KB + product snippets), use embeddings with cutoff similarity 0.78. 2) Retriever response condensation: short 2-3 bullet summary via a constrained generation model (Mistral-7B q4). 3) Instruction template: few-shot example set (3 examples) + instruction + condensed context + user query. 4) Safety and normalization: post-process to strip PII placeholders and canonicalize SKUs. 5) Final short completion with temperature 0.0-0.2 for deterministic SKU lookup, 0.6 for creative copywrites. Streaming enabled for long outputs but chunk size limited to 32 tokens per event.
quality_tradeoffs: Quantization trades: q4_0 loses some subtle fuzzy-match recall (rare synonyms) — mitigated by adding paraphrase examples in prompt and increasing retrieval context window. 13B variants slightly better on edge-case factual corrections but cost/latency hit. Mixed-mode quant with KV in 8-bit keeps decode fast and preserves some numeric stability.
routing_and_fallback_policy:
- Primary route: Mistral-7B q4_0 on Dedicated pool (meets latency/cost).
- Fallbacks: If model error rate > threshold OR capacity constrained, route to Llama2-13B q8_dyn on high-tier nodes.
- Graceful degradation: switch to retrieval-only categorical SKU lookup (exact match table) if generation exceeds latency threshold > 350ms.
eval_plan_and_metrics: Offline eval: use 3 datasets: prod anonymized chat logs (2k turns), curated SKU match set (500 queries), and creative marketing prompts (200). Metrics: SKU exact match %, semantic recall @1, hallucination rate (manual label), BLEU not used. Production SLOs: SKU exact match >= 92%, p95 latency <= 220ms, hallucination rate <= 2% on support flows.
security_and_privacy_notes: All PII redaction done before vectors stored. Use customer KMS for private deployments. Recommendation: enable request-level logging with redaction hooks and per-token cost sampling turned off for EU customer until audit completed.
cost_estimates:
Estimated unit cost (based on microbench and current pricing):
- Mistral-7B q4_0: ~$0.0022 per 1k tokens (generation+embedding amortized)
- Llama2-13B q8_dyn: ~$0.0048 per 1k tokens
- Fallback retrieval-only path: negligible per-request (embedding cost for retrieval amortized)
These are rough; include 20% buffer for traffic bursts.
open_questions:
- Does customer require audit trail of exact model version used for every response? (affects routing metadata)
- Are there hard SLA implications on p50 vs p95 for checkout flows?
- Will customer permit any non-EU compute for batch evals?
decision_log: Sprint decision 2025-09-09: go-forward = Mistral-7B q4_0 on dedicated pool for default route + Llama2-13B q8_dyn as higher-accuracy fallback. Implement prefix caching for common KB queries. Owner: Jamal Chen.
runbook_snippets:
- Latency alarm: p95 > 280ms for 5m -> auto-scale + notify on-call.
- Quality alarm: SKU exact match drop > 4 percentage points vs baseline -> automatic rollback to fp16 dev snapshot and open incident.
- Manual steps: to force fallback route set routing tag 'use-13b' in request headers.
